newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't to free funds for agriculture - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't to free funds for agriculture - paper.

text.p: Brazil's government may raise its financing limit for sugar cane, soybean, sorghum and coffee harvests to 150,000 reais per farmer from 30,000 reais, financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said.

Gazeta, quoting Agriculture Ministry Policy Secretary Guilherme Leite Dias, said the government also plans to reduce farm interest rates to nine percent a year from 10 percent and adjust minimum prices upward four to seven percent.
The moves are part of a package of measures contained in the government's Harvest Plan due to be released by Agriculture Minister Arlindo Porto in the first half of June, the paper said.
It said the crop financing limit of 150,000 reais per producer is now available only to growers of beans, corn, manioc and wheat.
"We're thinking about expanding this benefit to sugar cane, soybeans, sorghum and coffee," the paper quoted Dias as saying.

He added it is mostly likely going to be extended to sorghum while sugar cane, coffee and soybeans may face more opposition because they are export crops and producers are numerous and absorb much rural credit.
"This will cause an explosion in demand for financing," Dias was quoted as saying.
Dias added the government has not decided what crops it will raise minimum prices for.
